extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, senior reviewers, and academic institutions responsible for training peer reviewers; also junior reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for recruiting, training, supervising, and graduating junior peer reviewers (a proposed 'reviewer residency' and related modalities) to sustain timely, high-quality academic peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for reviewer training
rubrics_metrics.description: Producing peer reviewers with high caliber is time-consuming and necessary; an experienced author does not invariably make a good reviewer, indicating the need for formal reviewer training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training programs should be effective, logistically affordable, and demonstrate long-lasting positive impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goals: reduce delays and bias; increase reviewer pool
rubrics_metrics.description: Delayed and/or biased peer reviews are key contributors to concerns about the integrity and efficiency of peer review; reviewers' competing commitments contribute to delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate and mentor junior academics to create a larger, competent pool of reviewers to improve timeliness and reduce burden on senior reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Open peer review: the reviewer’s identity is known to the readers and the author; reviewer reports are published alongside the accepted manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open peer review makes reviewer reports educational (both factual content and analytical approach) for potential future reviewers and preserves useful discussions that would otherwise be lost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-review (mentored reviewing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-review denotes when a non-invited reviewer (usually a postgraduate student) contributes ideas or writing during a review under supervision of a senior researcher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-reviewing improves novice competency; journals can invite reviewers to collaborate with junior researchers, permit recognition (e.g., adding co-reviewers to Publons), and make co-reviewing part of regular practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to other reviewers' assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowing junior reviewers to view the reviews of other reviewers allocated to the same manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visibility of senior reviewers' reports lets juniors learn analytical approaches and improve their own reviews (e.g., Cureus practice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial feedback and quality assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing feedback and quality assessment by the editor to reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers responded positively to editor feedback as a way to improve their reviews; authors suggest need for more detailed editorial feedback. Evidence indicates editorial feedback can improve performance, but long-term effects require sustained follow-up and mentoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured training programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal, structured training sessions/courses designed to teach peer-review skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structured programs have been used, but randomized and controlled studies show modest or no persistent improvements; long-term mentorship may be required for durable effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-instructional review packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Standalone self-directed materials for learning how to perform peer reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-instructional packages produced modest improvements in error identification but failed to demonstrate persistent improvements in review quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online learning modules combined with co-review
rubrics_metrics.description: Online modules providing instruction followed by supervised co-review with a senior reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by some journals; similar to other methods, evidence for sustained improvement is limited, but pairing with supervision may increase value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshops for reviewer training
rubrics_metrics.description: Live or structured workshops to teach peer-review skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workshops can be effective but pose logistical problems and have reduced access to a wide circle of junior reviewers; scalability is limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer residency — staged training concept
rubrics_metrics.description: A multi-stage 'reviewer residency' adopted by journals: stepwise training, assessment, and progression to independent reviewing under mentorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Residency integrates co-review, supervised independent review, and unsupervised independent review; recommended to be adapted per journal with senior reviewer/editor as supervisor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting potential reviewers by willingness
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial recruitment of candidates should be based on voluntary desire to undergo reviewer residency rather than expertise and experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals can provide opportunities to authors who state willingness to be reviewers; selection emphasizes motivation and availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigning a senior reviewer/editor mentor
rubrics_metrics.description: Each new reviewer should be paired with a senior reviewer or editor who supervises their training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentors may supervise several new reviewers depending on commitments, or be assigned one trainee; mentor responsibility includes providing feedback and assessing readiness for progression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial co-review stage (start simple, use standard format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Junior reviewer is given an uncomplicated manuscript (case reports, simple protocols) to review using a standard review format assessing basic manuscript components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senior reviewer completes their review on the same manuscript and discusses improvements with the trainee; acceptable trainee comments can be sent to authors and trainees informed about re-review if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progressive increase in manuscript complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign gradually more complex manuscripts (complex protocols, study designs, data analysis, review articles) as the trainee progresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If trainees need additional expertise (e.g., statistics), direct them to appropriate personnel (statisticians) and provide necessary software; complexity should increase as competency grows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervised independent review stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainee performs independent reviews supervised by the mentor; the number of manuscripts for co-review/transition is jointly decided by mentor and trainee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By this stage, trainee comments are revised only if required before submission to authors; trainees should also receive comments from other external reviewers at this stage to aid learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsupervised independent review stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainee has mastered skills and knowledge to conduct quality peer review independently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At this final stage the reviewer conducts reviews without ongoing mentor oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide trainee access to external reviewer comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Junior reviewers should be provided with comments from other external peer reviewers during co-review and supervised stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exposure to other reviewers' comments contributes to skill improvement and understanding of review standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication channels to minimize delay
rubrics_metrics.description: Use email, mobile phone applications, and online real-time communication apps to enable communication between senior reviewers and mentees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Online communication minimizes delays in feedback and speeds mentor-trainee interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition, incentives, and retention strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide incentives such as reviewer/co-reviewer acknowledgments, inclusion of reviewer names in published manuscripts, waivers for authorship submissions, and certificates for residency completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incentives motivate and retain reviewers across seniority levels; certificates accepted in academia increase program acceptance and demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Send trainee reviews to authors when acceptable
rubrics_metrics.description: If trainee reviews are of acceptable quality, these reviewer comments can be sent to the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides real-world impact for trainees and reinforces standards; mentors should ensure quality before sending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practicality and sustainability considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Although reviewer training programs might be impractical for some journals, persistent editorial/senior reviewer mentorship can have sustained positive effects and lead to a self-sustaining pool of competent reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals should consider modern technology (free communication apps, software) to overcome practical difficulties; long-term commitment is required for durable improvements.
